prize_parts.citation: For the invention and realization of optical lattice clocks, from the magic-wavelength trapping of many neutral atoms to clocks of unprecedented accuracy and stability

statement.case_for: I keep the single-part prize for optical lattice clocks to Katori and Ye, and I have not changed my preferred configuration since round 1. The reason is the criterion I stated in my March lecture, as reported by Tohoku: a prize is for a discovery or invention, and the committee must be able to name the topic and the people responsible for the original work. Here the topic is narrow and specific: a trapping wavelength at which the light shift cancels for the clock transition, so that many neutral atoms can be interrogated at once, followed by realizations at roughly 1e-18. The two names map onto the two parts of that sentence, the concept and early strontium clocks, and the record-setting realization. Independent reproduction in strontium and ytterbium in several laboratories settles maturity, and the consequences are measurable in tests of constants, relativistic geodesy and the preparation of a redefinition of the second. After reading the chair's summary I also see that the round has narrowed to two single-part options with no shared laureates, and that the disagreement is about names and framing, not about the worth of either discovery. I prefer B013 because its attribution can be defended name by name, not because I think it outweighs the Higgs observation in significance; I said that in round 1 and I repeat it.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is unchanged: overlap with the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes, which a sceptic can read as a third prize in one metrology line. I think the answer is that the lattice scheme addresses a different problem from either, but the citation has to carry that argument, and a broad wording such as precision optical clocks would invite the incrementalism objection. The two-name allocation also leaves out real contributors (Lemonde and the Paris group, the German groups, the NIST and JILA team members, Takamoto, and the ion-clock pioneers). The redefinition of the second has not yet happened, so part of the payoff is prospective. The larger cost is the one Danielsson, Johansson and Pearce name: passing over the Higgs discovery, which has had no experimental recognition since 2013, for a narrower result. I accept that cost and would reverse my preference only if the Higgs supporters can state a rule that selects three names and that I can defend in a public citation.

responses.point: Danielsson holds the Higgs discovery first with Gianotti, Jenni and Virdee, argues that attribution is a leadership judgement, says he would move to Della Negra if founding conception were shown to outweigh leadership at the time of the discovery, and treats B013 as the right fallback if no trio can be agreed.
responses.response: I take your willingness to move between Virdee and Della Negra as the honest statement of where the Higgs case stands, but it is also the problem. A rule that can be satisfied by either name is not yet a rule. The two principles on the table select different trios: founding conception gives Della Negra and Jenni, announcement-time leadership gives Gianotti and Virdee, and Gianotti alone satisfies both. Under any single principle applied consistently, one of the four is excluded for a reason that the excluded person's collaboration will contest. I would only move to B001 if you and Pearce agree on one trio and the one-sentence principle behind it before the vote. Your fallback to B013 is welcome, since it means we do not disagree about the clocks, only about the order.

responses.point: Mehlig moved to B013 from the Higgs, keeps B001 as her first alternative, would support it if the committee can agree a principled rule such as the ATLAS and CMS founding leaders plus one spokesperson, and does not want the citation to claim that lattice clocks are the only path to 1e-18.
responses.response: I agree with your last point and would build it into the citation. It should name the magic-wavelength lattice and the neutral-atom realization, and it should not imply that ion clocks or other routes are lesser or that lattice clocks are the sole path to this level. On your proposed rule, founding leaders plus one spokesperson, I note that it yields four names for a three-person cap as soon as you count two founders and the spokespersons on both sides, so it does not by itself settle the allocation either. I would be more persuaded by a rule that also says why the fourth person is not credited. Our difference remains one of ordering, since we both keep the Higgs as the first alternative.

responses.point: Pearce, as chair, asked whether a two-part prize combining B001 and B013 is worth considering given the three-laureate cap, and in his own statement ranks the Higgs first because the 2013 prize left the experiment unrecognised, while seeing B013 as a continuation of recognised metrology.
responses.response: I looked at the two-part option because it is the only way to honour both results. I would exclude it. With at most three people in total and Katori and Ye needed for B013, the Higgs part would be left with a single name, and one name for a two-experiment discovery is the least defensible attribution of all. The alternative, giving the clocks one name, would separate the concept from its realization. So I see the choice as real: one prize or the other. On your point that 2005 and 2012 make this the third prize in a metrology line, I read it as showing that the Academy has already judged this lineage prize-worthy, and the question for the citation is only what is new, which is many-atom interrogation free of light-shift error. I would ask that the chair record the sequence of the vote so the Higgs configuration is tested first if the supporters bring a single trio.

responses.point: Kroll opened B013 first, argues that the lattice clock is a distinct enabling idea, and discloses a possible perceived tie to John Hall's laboratory, with which Jun Ye is associated, saying the committee may wish to consider recusal on B013.
responses.response: I appreciate the disclosure and agree it is a perceived tie, not a documented conflict. The chair's summary records that Eriksson and Mehlig note that the support for B013 does not depend on your ballot, and I can add that I ranked it third at opening and moved to it after reading others, independently of your argument. I would nevertheless want the record to show it, and I would suggest the committee ask you to state whether the Hall-laboratory stay overlapped with Ye's time there and whether you collaborated with him. That is a factual question, and the answer should decide whether recusal is needed, not a general concern. I would not ask for recusal on the information we have, but I would not object if you chose it.

responses.point: Johansson keeps the Higgs first with Gianotti, Della Negra and Jenni, treats B013 as a serious alternative and not a token one, and recuses himself from B054 given his link to WACQT.
responses.response: Your statement that you regard B013 as a serious fallback matters for the vote, because it means that B013 can gather a large majority if the Higgs trio cannot be agreed. I also thank you for keeping to your recusal on B054. I do not think the Chalmers connection between us bears on B013 or B001, and I note that neither of us has a documented tie to the credited names on those ballots. On Virdee versus Della Negra I have no private information that would choose between them, and my own earlier trio was Gianotti, Della Negra and Jenni, so I am sympathetic to your weighting of founding conception, but I do not think a founding-based rule can be shown to win over a spokesperson-based rule from the evidence we have.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will see optical lattice clocks as a distinct invention or as a continuation of the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes, which depends on how narrowly the citation is worded.
Whether Katori and Ye alone adequately represent the people responsible, given the Paris, German and NIST/JILA contributions that are not in the credited names.
Whether the Higgs supporters can agree on one trio and a stated principle; if they can, I would weigh B001 against B013 again on significance.
Whether the pending redefinition of the second will have taken place or be firmly scheduled by the time of the decision.
My account of dates and individual roles is recalled from memory and not verified against primary sources.
statement.conflict_note: I am an electron microscopist and past president (2024) of the International Federation of Societies for Microscopy, so I have a close subject-matter link to B015 (aberration-corrected electron optics), my own opening first place, which I no longer advocate and would recuse myself from if it came up. Göran Johansson is a fellow Chalmers professor, which matters only for his disclosed link to B054. No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for B013, B001 or B046, and none of Katori, Ye, Gianotti, Della Negra, Jenni, Virdee, Bistritzer, MacDonald or Jarillo-Herrero is a documented colleague. I note Kroll's disclosed Hall-laboratory link as his own flag, not mine.
